drawdown_context: GO FY24 10-K (filed Feb 26, 2025) discloses sharp business deterioration: comp sales decelerated from 11.8% (FY22) -> 7.5% (FY23) -> 2.7% (FY24); FY24 comp growth was decomposed as +4.2% transactions / -1.4% ticket (consumer trading down within an already extreme-value banner). Gross margin compressed 110bps to 30.2%. Adjusted net income fell 29.4% YoY despite 10.1% net sales growth (mostly inorganic from the 40-store United Grocery Outlet acquisition closed Apr 1 2024 + 27 new openings). Management initiated a Restructuring Plan in Q4 FY24 ($52-61M total cost) involving termination of 23 already-signed leases for stores planned in FY25/26, cancellation of certain capex-intensive warehouse projects, and a Feb 18 2025 RIF of ~40 corporate FTEs. The 10-K also discloses an UNREMEDIATED material weakness in ICFR (ITGCs around the Aug 2023 ERP replacement) AND that BOTH the CFO and the CEO had been replaced during FY24/FY25 (the 10-K is the first signed by new CEO Jason Potter). Pre-cutoff 10-Q (filed May 7, 2025) confirmed continued comp deceleration to +0.3% (Q1 FY25) with transactions +2.3% / ticket -2.0%, and FY25 comp guidance was CUT from 2.0-3.0% to 1.0-2.0%. -42.6% forward return reflects the market's ex-post recognition that the IO commission-support cost (which began Q3 FY23) is structural, the ERP-related shrink/inventory drag is persistent, and the new-store growth engine has been turned off.

rfm_tuples.R: FY24 10-K MD&A: 'Comparable store sales increased 2.7%, driven by a 4.2% increase in the number of transactions, partially offset by a 1.4% decrease in average transaction size.' Brand narrative: 'positive comparable store sales for over 20 years, with the exception of fiscal 2021.'
rfm_tuples.f: self_text decomposition of comp sales (traffic x ticket) over multi-year window; Mode B: did the next 10-Q reinforce or reverse the traffic-positive / ticket-negative pattern (i.e. trading-down)?
rfm_tuples.M_value: Multi-year comp trajectory: FY22 +11.8% -> FY23 +7.5% -> FY24 +2.7% -> Q1 FY25 +0.3% (10-Q filed 2025-05-07). Ticket size went from -1.4% (FY24) to -2.0% (Q1 FY25); traffic decelerated 4.2% -> 2.3%. Pre-cutoff 10-Q narrative attributes the comp miss partly to 'timing shift of the Easter holiday' (a soft excuse) but management CUT FY25 comp guidance from 2.0-3.0% to 1.0-2.0% in the May 6 2025 earnings release.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B catches the trading-down signal: at an extreme-value retailer, NEGATIVE ticket size during a recessionary tape is a tell that the customer is buying smaller baskets even at GO's price point. Combined with traffic deceleration (4.2% -> 2.3%) and a same-quarter guidance cut, the 'consistent comp growth' brand-equity claim in the 10-K was visibly fraying at the time of filing.

rfm_tuples.R: FY24 10-K: 'To alleviate the disruption caused by the system upgrades that we implemented in late August 2023... we elected to provide commission support to IOs beginning in the third quarter of fiscal 2023... extending through fiscal 2024. We continue to provide minimal commission support to IOs for inventory.' Independent Operator model: 'We generally share 50% of store-level gross profits with IOs.'
rfm_tuples.f: self_text on IO commission support evolution (started Q3 FY23, framed as 'temporary' through FY24, then '_continued at minimal level_' in 10-Q); Mode B: a 'temporary' support payment now in its 7th consecutive quarter is structural, and gross-margin compression is the visible footprint.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Commission support has now run Q3 FY23 -> Q4 FY23 -> all of FY24 -> Q1 FY25 = 7+ quarters. 10-K acknowledges 'continued provid[ing] minimal commission support to IOs for inventory.' Gross margin compressed from 31.3% (FY23) to 30.2% (FY24); the IO economic damage is sufficient that the 10-K added a risk factor: 'inability to retain qualified IOs; failure of our IOs to successfully manage their business; failure of our IOs to repay notes outstanding to us.' IO notes-receivable allowance grew from $11.2M to $11.8M YoY (modest but elevated provision in 10-Q $3.3M vs $0.6M y/y).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 'IO commission support is temporary' framing is being walked back without explicit retraction. If the support is structural, the 50/50 gross-profit split is effectively a 55/45 split favoring the IO, which is permanent margin damage. The 10-Q's elevated IO accounts-receivable provision ($3.3M vs $0.6M) is a Mode B confirmation that IO unit economics are deteriorating fast enough to require write-down.

rfm_tuples.R: FY24 10-K Restructuring Plan: 'terminate 23 leases for unopened stores in suboptimal locations, 15 of which we had planned to open in fiscal 2025 and eight of which we had planned to open in fiscal 2026' AND 'we are revising our near-term new store growth strategy.' Historical store growth: 441 (FY22) -> 468 (FY23) -> 533 (FY24, of which 40 were UGO acquired). FY24 new openings: 27.
rfm_tuples.f: self_text on Restructuring Plan disclosure quantifying the new-store growth scaling-back; Mode B: termination of 23 already-signed leases means new-store unit economics had deteriorated SO MUCH that breaking the lease and eating a $29M lease-termination charge was cheaper than opening the store.
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-Q (May 2025): $29.1M of lease termination costs incurred in Q1 FY25 (largest restructuring line item); FY25 new store guidance: 33-35 net new (vs 27 organic in FY24 — flat-ish but down from the prior growth trajectory). 10-Q: 'planned new store openings have been reduced from previous expectations in connection with the Restructuring Plan.' Total restructuring cost guided $59-61M with $40-42M cash.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The unit-growth narrative — historically GO's bull thesis — is broken. Breaking 23 signed leases (not just declining to sign new ones) is the most expensive way to throttle growth and signals that pro-forma store-level returns had crashed below cost-of-lease-termination. The 10-K obscures the per-store economics that drove the decision; it lets readers infer the magnitude from the dollar charge but does not show new-store payback periods.

rfm_tuples.R: FY24 10-K: 'we replaced components of our enterprise resource planning system, including our financial ledger, inventory management platform and product data warehouse system. The implementation of these system upgrades resulted in significant ordering and inventory disruptions during fiscal 2023 and fiscal 2024.' Item 9A: 'our internal control over financial reporting was not effective as of December 28, 2024' due to a material weakness in ITGCs unremediated from FY23.
rfm_tuples.f: auditor_change_from_text + going_concern_local + claim_evolution on material weakness remediation status
rfm_tuples.M_value: Material weakness FIRST disclosed in FY23 10-K (related to Aug 2023 ERP cutover); FY24 10-K confirms 'we did not achieve our prior expectation to be able to remediate such material weakness by the end of fiscal 2024.' 'Corrective controls were implemented during the fiscal year ending December 28, 2024, but need to continue operating effectively for a sufficient period of time to conclude the material weakness has been remediated.' Auditor (Deloitte) issued an adverse opinion on ICFR. 10-Q acknowledges remediation 'is ongoing' as of March 29, 2025. Deloitte tenure stable — no auditor change.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: A material weakness extending 16+ months past the ERP cutover, with management missing its own remediation timeline, signals that the inventory-management system and shrink-control problems are still degrading store-level execution. This directly links to the IO commission-support cost (necessitated by IOs being unable to order/manage inventory correctly), the gross-margin compression, and the elevated shrink. Auditor remained Deloitte through both years (positive disclosure-quality signal), but the underlying control failure is structurally bad.

rfm_tuples.R: FY24 10-K Note 2: 'shrink' defined as 'markdowns, throwaways and theft'; IOs split shrink 50/50, but 'excessive levels of shrink are deducted from commissions paid to IOs.' Risk factor: 'Since the implementation of system upgrades in August 2023, we and our IOs have experienced significant issues with ordering, inventory planning and management and payment processing, including our ability to accurately forecast sales.' Gross margin: 30.2% FY24 vs 31.3% FY23 (-110 bps).
rfm_tuples.f: self_text on gross-margin trajectory + inventory disclosures; Mode B: does the next 10-Q's gross margin improve as the ERP stabilizes, or has shrink become structural?
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 FY25 gross margin was 30.4% (10-Q) vs Q1 FY24 29.3% — a 110bps Y/Y improvement, but Q1 FY24 was the trough quarter. FY24 full-year GM (30.2%) vs FY23 (31.3%) shows the inventory-management problem is structurally compressing margin by ~100bps. 10-Q narrative: 'tighter inventory management' was the main driver of the modest sequential GM recovery.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Gross margin has not recovered to the pre-ERP baseline (FY22 was 31.0%+ range). The combination of structural IO commission support + persistent shrink/inventory drag means GO is operating with ~100 bps less gross profit than its pre-2023 self — on a 30% GM business, that's a third of operating margin gone. The 10-K downplays this by emphasizing the y/y comparison (FY24 vs FY23) rather than the level (FY24 vs FY22/pre-ERP).

rfm_tuples.R: FY24 10-K: UGO acquired Apr 1 2024 for $62.5M cash, adding 40 stores in TN/NC/GA/AL/KY/VA. 'The goodwill recognized reflects the expected future benefits from certain synergies and intangible assets that do not qualify for separate recognition.' Goodwill grew $34.8M from the deal. 10-K: 'the impact of the United Grocery Outlet stores in aggregate were not material to our operations.' UGO stores remain company-operated (not IO-converted).
rfm_tuples.f: self_text on UGO economic contribution + integration status; Mode B: did the company convert UGO stores to the IO model on the disclosed timeline, or are they stuck operating as company-stores (a different economic model)?
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY24 10-K (filed Feb 2025): of the 533 total stores, 42 were company-operated, 'including the 40 acquired United Grocery Outlet stores' — i.e. NONE had been converted to IO model. 10-Q (May 2025): 543 total stores 'as of March 29, 2025... 42 were Company-operated stores' — same number, still no IO conversions. Goodwill on balance sheet at Dec 28 2024 = $884M gross / $826M net — UGO added $34.8M to goodwill. Stock has fallen from ~$22 at deal close (Apr 2024) to ~$14 at cutoff = -36% during the period the acquisition would be tested for impairment.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B finding: the IO-conversion plan is the main synergy thesis (IO stores have higher returns than company-operated), and zero of the 40 UGO stores had been converted 11 months post-close. If the integration is stalled, the goodwill impairment risk is real — but the 10-K only states '_we evaluate the timing to transition_' rather than committing. Note GO's market-cap-to-book ratio at cutoff was approaching unity (stock at $14 against ~$13/share book value), suggesting the market was pricing some goodwill impairment risk. Material weakness in ICFR adds risk that impairment triggers go unnoticed.

rfm_tuples.R: FY24 10-K: 'During fiscal 2024, we repurchased 3,977,163 shares at an average repurchase price per share of $20.23' = $80.4M. Nov 2024: Board approved NEW $100M share repurchase program (replacing 2021 program), $100M still authorized at year-end. CapEx FY24 = $206.9M (gross) / $185.7M (net of TIA); FY25 guidance $210M.
rfm_tuples.f: self_text on buyback execution price vs current trading price + new authorization timing; Mode B: did management buy back stock at $20+ while business was clearly deteriorating, and then approve a NEW $100M program even as the Restructuring Plan was being initiated?
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY24 buybacks: 3.98M shares @ $20.23 avg = $80.4M. Stock price at cutoff (May 15 2025) = $13.97 — 31% below the avg buyback price. Q4 FY24 buybacks alone: 1.51M shares @ $16.62 (deteriorated economics already visible). Nov 2024 board authorized ANOTHER $100M repurchase program — concurrent with initiation of the Restructuring Plan and elevated capex. No buybacks executed in Q1 FY25 per the 10-Q cash-flow statement (financing activities show no share repurchases line for the 13-week period, only the $5.6M sched. term loan payment and other items).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Classic capital-misallocation pattern: heavy buybacks at peak multiples ($20+) while inventory/IO/ERP problems were already manifest in declining comp growth (FY24 +2.7% vs FY23 +7.5%). Management paused buybacks in Q1 FY25 — suggesting they recognized the misallocation — but the $100M new authorization remains undeployed and is a moot signal given the leverage covenant headroom is shrinking.

rfm_tuples.R: FY24 10-K Note 6: 2023 Credit Agreement = $300M term loan ($288.8M outstanding) + $400M revolver ($190M drawn). Max Total Net Leverage covenant = 3.50x through Q4 FY25, stepping down to 3.25x thereafter. Min Interest Coverage = 1.75x. Term loan matures Feb 2028. FY24 Adj EBITDA = $236.8M (down 6.3% YoY).
rfm_tuples.f: self_text on covenant headroom: implied debt/(Adj EBITDA) ratio at year-end + Mode B: is the Restructuring Plan's $40-42M cash cost going to be added back to covenant EBITDA, or does it eat headroom?
rfm_tuples.M_value: Year-end FY24 net debt (term loan $288.8M + revolver $190M - cash ~$62M = ~$417M). Adj EBITDA $236.8M -> implied Net Leverage ~1.76x. Covenant max 3.50x = ~$830M of debt capacity at current EBITDA. Headroom appears comfortable on paper. BUT: revolver utilization grew $190M during FY24 ($0 at start of FY23) to fund UGO + buybacks; interest expense $33.1M in FY25 vs ~$11M in FY22; 10-Q Q1 FY25 interest expense $6.5M (Q1 only) = $26M annualized. Covenant EBITDA add-backs for restructuring charges allowed but capped. Most material risk: FY25 Adj EBITDA guidance $260-270M — if comp guidance midpoint of 1.5% comes in lower, EBITDA could miss and leverage could climb toward 2.5x — still below covenant but visibly weaker.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Covenant headroom is real (no near-term breach risk) and the 10-K disclosure of the covenant terms is accurate. This is the one balance-sheet area where GO does NOT signal distress — explains why no going-concern language. The 12-month forward maturity risk is minimal: term loan matures 2028. This is the principal reason the framework would NOT flag GO as a Wolfspeed-style imminent-distress short.

rfm_tuples.R: FY24 10-K Item 9A and Exhibit 23.1: Deloitte & Touche LLP as independent auditor. Adverse opinion on ICFR effectiveness due to unremediated material weakness; unqualified opinion on the financial statements.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Deterministic check (local + Edgar): signal=CLEAN_AUDITOR_TENURE; n_8k_item_401 = 0; n_big4_resignations = 0; n_disagreements = 0. Deloitte signed both the financial-statements opinion and the (adverse) ICFR opinion. No auditor change pre-cutoff.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: No auditor-change signal. Deloitte continuing to engage despite the unremediated material weakness is mildly positive on disclosure-quality dimension. This + clean going-concern axis = the framework does not produce a fraud/distress flag on accounting-governance grounds.

rfm_tuples.R: FY24 10-K: 'In fiscal 2024 and fiscal 2025, we completed thorough and external searches for a new Chief Financial Officer and a new President and Chief Executive Officer, respectively, following the departure of their predecessors. We utilized interim officers to serve in such capacities for a period of time as well.' New CEO Jason Potter onboard.
rfm_tuples.f: form4 / insider_vs_calendar around 10-K filing (Feb 26, 2025) — does management put MONEY behind the turnaround thesis, or sell? CRITICAL: distinguish discretionary open-market purchases (P/A) from sell-to-cover tax withholding sales (S/D with footnote disclosure)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Pre-cutoff Form 4 transactions in days after the 10-K filing (Feb 26 - Mar 15 2025) — distinguishing P (open-market purchase) from S (sale): OPEN-MARKET PURCHASES (CONVICTION SIGNAL): (a) Erik Ragatz [director, Hellman & Friedman affiliate] purchased 165,000 shares @ $12.25 on 2025-02-28 = ~$2.02M; (b) Christopher Miller [new CFO] purchased 10,000 shares @ $11.68 on 2025-02-27 = ~$117K; (c) Kenneth Alterman [director] purchased 25,000 shares @ $11.88 on 2025-03-03 = ~$297K; (d) John Bachman [director] purchased 14,000 shares @ $11.36 on 2025-03-04 = ~$159K; (e) Carey Jaros [director] purchased 5,000 shares @ $11.40 on 2025-03-04 = ~$57K. TOTAL pre-cutoff insider OPEN-MARKET BUYS ~$2.65M across 5 distinct insiders (incl. 4 directors + new CFO) within 5 trading days of the 10-K. SALES were ALL sell-to-cover for PSU/RSU tax withholding per Form 4 footnotes (Lindberg, Wilson, Burke, Thompson, Gray, Bortner, Chikkala on Mar 4 & Mar 10 = ~$1.0M of sales tied to vesting events, NOT discretionary sales). Net insider activity = +$2.65M PURCHASE / -$1.0M tax-withholding = clearly POSITIVE.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B finding that flips the conventional read: when one ignores the tax-withholding sales (which are mechanical), a fresh CFO + four sitting directors collectively committed $2.65M of personal capital at $11-12 within days of the 10-K. Hellman & Friedman's representative on the board (Ragatz) putting $2M to work is the strongest insider-buy signal in this dataset — H&F took GO public and knows the model. This is a clean COUNTER-signal to the otherwise negative business trajectory. RECONCILES with the ex-post -42.6% return how? The insiders were wrong — they bought a value trap. From a framework standpoint, this is a CASE where the insider signal is misleading; the structural business deterioration (IO support permanence, ERP shrink, comp deceleration, ticket negative) is the operative truth.

rfm_tuples.R: FY24 10-K Item 11 / CEO statement: 'In fiscal 2024 and fiscal 2025, we completed thorough and external searches for a new Chief Financial Officer and a new President and Chief Executive Officer... following the departure of their predecessors. We utilized interim officers to serve in such capacities for a period of time as well.' RJ Sheedy (prior CEO) departed; Jason Potter [former Sobeys exec] hired. New CFO Chris Miller. New 10-K mentions: 'commencing a search for a new Store Operations leader, along with other key management roles.'
rfm_tuples.f: self_text + claim_evolution: simultaneous CFO + CEO departures within ~12 months is high-tier governance/operational red flag; new CEO's first 10-K is also the one initiating the Restructuring Plan
rfm_tuples.M_value: CFO change + CEO change + announcement (in May 2025 Q1 earnings release) of a search for new Store Operations leader + 'other key management roles.' Within 18 months, GO had replaced (i) the CEO, (ii) the CFO, (iii) was searching for Store Ops EVP, (iv) had reduced corporate headcount by 40 FTEs. The 10-K language ('utilized interim officers to serve in such capacities') euphemistically describes a period of headless leadership during the ERP crisis.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Triple-replacement at the top of a retailer mid-crisis is a high-tier negative signal. The new CEO had been in seat ~6 months at 10-K filing (his Form 4 award of 168,492 RSUs is dated Feb 28, 2025 — that's his inducement grant). New management teams typically take 2-3 quarters to diagnose then 2-3 more to execute. The market's -42.6% subsequent return reflects the realization that the turnaround will take longer than the 12-month forward horizon and that the structural margin damage (IO support, ERP shrink) is harder to reverse than presented.

rfm_tuples.R: Specific 10-K claims to test against the 10-Q (filed May 7, 2025, 8 days pre-cutoff): (a) 'comparable store sales increased 2.7%' (FY24) -> reaffirm trajectory? (b) 'Restructuring Plan total cost $52-61M' -> hold or revised? (c) FY25 outlook (implicit in MD&A) -> reaffirm or revise? (d) IO commission support 'minimal' -> still minimal?
rfm_tuples.f: claim_evolution between 10-K (Feb 26 2025) and 10-Q (May 7 2025) — quantify the dispositive deltas
rfm_tuples.M_value: (a) Comp sales Q1 FY25 = +0.3% (vs FY24 +2.7%) - sharp deceleration; (b) Restructuring cost revised UP from $52-61M to $59-61M (mid-point up ~6%), cash component up to $40-42M from $36-45M; (c) FY25 COMP GUIDANCE CUT from 2.0-3.0% to 1.0-2.0% in May 6 8-K (midpoint -1.0%); (d) IO commission support continued in Q1 (still on the books). 10-Q operating loss $22.5M vs Q1 FY24 $0.6M operating income — material deterioration even excluding the $33.9M restructuring charge.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B signal — between Feb 26 (10-K) and May 6 (Q1 earnings), management cut comp guidance, raised restructuring cost estimates, and posted an operating loss. All three deltas are negative. The 10-K's FY25 implicit setup was visibly off-base within 10 weeks of filing. Framework's claim_evolution check correctly flags this as material negative-direction revision.

summary: GO's FY24 10-K (filed Feb 26, 2025) was a moderately honest distress disclosure that explicitly initiated a Restructuring Plan, kept Deloitte as auditor, and admitted an unremediated material weakness. But it materially underdelivered on three priority dimensions for the survivorship-backtest framework: (1) MULTI-YEAR COMP DECELERATION (11.8% -> 7.5% -> 2.7% -> 0.3% Q1 FY25) with NEGATIVE ticket size (-1.4% FY24, -2.0% Q1 FY25) — Mode B catches consumer trading down INSIDE an extreme-value retailer; (2) IO COMMISSION SUPPORT framed as 'temporary' for 7+ consecutive quarters — structurally permanent margin damage masked by 'minimal' language; (3) NEW-STORE GROWTH THROTTLED via termination of 23 already-signed leases at $29.1M Q1 cost (the unit-growth bull thesis is broken). Auditor (Deloitte) clean tenure + adequate covenant headroom (1.76x vs 3.50x max; term loan due 2028) explains the absence of going-concern language and the framework's deterministic NO_GOING_CONCERN signal. Mode B INSIDER COUNTER-SIGNAL: $2.65M of open-market buys by H&F director Ragatz ($2.0M) + 3 other directors + new CFO Miller within 5 trading days of the 10-K (discretionary sales = $0; all 'S' transactions were PSU tax withholding per footnotes); insiders were WRONG ex-post. Triple top-management turnover (CEO, CFO, Store Ops in search) during ERP-driven operational crisis is the highest-tier governance flag. Pre-cutoff 10-Q (May 7, 2025) confirmed comp guidance cut from 2.0-3.0% to 1.0-2.0%, raised restructuring cost estimates, posted Q1 operating loss. Framework should produce a NEGATIVE-WEAK rating: business deterioration signals dominate, but no going-concern / no auditor change / strong insider buying create real ambiguity — and the deterministic framework would NOT flag this as a Wolfspeed-style imminent-distress short. The -42.6% forward return is a value-trap outcome (insiders + market overestimated turnaround speed). Composite ~0.32 = mild SHORT/AVOID with high disagreement.
